title: Broker and Freight Forwarder Financial Responsibility, Final Rule (88 FR, Nov 16 2023)
claim: Rule effective 2024-01-16; immediate-suspension/insolvency provisions compliance 2025-01-16; 'assets readily available' and BMC-85 trustee eligibility compliance 2026-01-16. BMC-85 assets limited to cash, ILOCs from federally insured depository institutions, Treasury bonds. Suspension if security < $75,000 and not replenished within 7 calendar days of FMCSA notice. FMCSA est. ~1.3% of brokers (~429 in 2022) see a drawdown per year (implies ~33,000 brokers; our arithmetic).
excerpt: Paraphrase: if broker 'does not replenish funds within 7 calendar days after notice from FMCSA', FMCSA issues notification of suspension.
limitations: Read via govinfo (first ~100k chars). Broker count is our back-calculation from FMCSA's 1.3%/429 estimate, not a stated census.

title: Motus registration system notice (Phase II launch)
claim: Motus replaces URS for registration incl. property brokers; all new applicants must pass identity proofing (ID photo + selfie) and CLEAR business verification; minimum 8 business days initial review, flagged applications longer; BOC-3 process and MC docket numbers unchanged in Phase II; fees paid via Pay.gov (amounts not stated).
excerpt: Customers 'may expect a minimum timeframe of eight business days for the initial review and processing'.
limitations: Does not state the OP-1 fee amount. MC-number elimination proposed but not done as of notice date.

title: UCR Fee Brackets
claim: Brokers pay only Bracket 1: $46 for 2026 registration year (unchanged from 2025).
excerpt: Paraphrase: broker fee $46 in Bracket 1 (0-2 vehicles) for 2026.
limitations: Figure obtained via search-result summary of the official page; page not fetched directly.

title: Fees for the Unified Carrier Registration Plan and Agreement (2027 registration year)
claim: UCR fees rise ~20% for 2027; broker/Bracket-1 fee $46 -> $55.
excerpt: Paraphrase: smallest operators and freight brokers in Bracket 1 see annual fee rise from $46 to $55.
limitations: Via search summary; not fetched in full.

title: Freight Broker License guide
claim: OP-1 broker authority application carries a non-refundable $300 filing fee; BMC-84 $75,000 bond; processing 4-6 weeks (vendor claim).
excerpt: Paraphrase: OP-1 must include a non-refundable filing fee of $300.
limitations: Vendor marketing page; fmcsa.dot.gov returned HTTP 403 so the $300 fee could not be confirmed on the primary source.

title: Definitions of Broker and Bona Fide Agents; final guidance
claim: Dispatch services must obtain broker authority if any of seven factors apply (negotiate with shippers, take payment from broker/factor, allocate traffic among multiple carriers, solicit open market of carriers, etc.). Unauthorized brokerage penalties pursued via DOJ in federal court.
excerpt: A dispatch service that arranges transportation for multiple carriers and allocates traffic 'is not a bona fide agent and must obtain broker operating authority registration'.
limitations: Guidance, not binding law.

title: Broker transparency proposal heads to OMB
claim: FMCSA sent supplemental broker-transparency (49 CFR 371.3) proposal to OIRA on 2026-08-27; still a proposal as of Sept 30 2026; 2024 NPRM drew ~7,000 comments.
excerpt: Paraphrase: supplemental proposal sent to White House regulatory review Aug 27, 2026.
limitations: Via search summaries of trade press; not fetched; current publication status unconfirmed.

title: Q3 2026 earnings release
claim: Q3 2026: revenue $5.358B (+29.5%); NAST revenue $3.829B, NAST AGP $517.9M (~13.5% of revenue, our calc); TL volume +3.5%; linehaul rate/mile +31.5% vs cost/mile +33.5% YoY; AGP per TL shipment +17%; NAST adj. op margin 40.3% of AGP; NAST headcount -11.4%; Global Forwarding op margin 36.6%; pending acquisition of RXO.
excerpt: CEO: market 'continued to reflect a period of significant supply-driven tightening.'
limitations: Incumbent economics (largest U.S. broker); not new-entrant economics.

title: Form 10-Q for quarter ended Sept 30, 2026
claim: Balance sheet 9/30/2026: receivables $3,547M, contract assets $291M, accounts payable $1,938M, accrued transportation $236M. Our calc: ~61 days sales outstanding vs ~39 days payables on ~$4.55B quarterly purchased transportation => incumbent broker funds roughly 3 weeks of carrier cost.
excerpt: Paraphrase: receivables, net $3,547,181k; accounts payable $1,938,433k.
limitations: DSO/DPO are our approximations from quarter revenue/AGP; AP includes non-carrier items.

title: Q3 2026 results press release
claim: Brokerage revenue $1.433B; brokerage gross margin 12.6% vs 13.5% YoY; TL volume +3%; TL spot mix 51% vs 29% YoY; definitive agreement (2026-10-05) to be acquired by C.H. Robinson, implied value $5.8B, close expected 1H 2027.
excerpt: 'Truckload spot mix was 51% of volume in the quarter'
limitations: Incumbent; margin compression reflects contract freight squeezed by rising carrier costs.

title: Q3 2026 earnings release
claim: Q3 2026 revenue $1,511.8M; purchased transportation 78.2% of revenue; commissions to agents $117.7M = 7.8% of revenue; insurance & claims $55.3M vs $33.0M; truck revenue/load $2,811 vs $2,245; BCO trucks 8,709; truck brokerage carriers 54% of revenue.
excerpt: Paraphrase: commissions to agents $117,676k on revenue $1,511,787k.
limitations: Agent-model incumbent; commission % is an average across agents of very different sizes.

title: Form 10-K FY2025
claim: ~960 independent commission sales agents; 457 'Million Dollar Agents' = 95% of revenue; >70,000 third-party capacity providers; agents paid contractual % of revenue or revenue less purchased transportation; operating subsidiaries (not agents) contract with customers and generally assume credit risk.
excerpt: Paraphrase: 'the Operating Subsidiaries, and not the Company's agents, contract directly with customers.'
limitations: Only first ~100k chars read.

title: DAT: Van spot rate rises to $3.05 a mile, highest since early 2022
claim: Oct 2026 national averages: van spot $3.05 (+$0.98 YoY) vs contract $3.28; reefer spot $3.60 vs contract $3.62; flatbed spot $3.61 vs contract $4.05; TVI van -2% YoY, reefer -9%, flatbed -7%; brokers paid carriers ~$1/mile more YoY; equipment posts 22-26% below last year.
excerpt: Carriers are heading into the holiday season 'in a position to be selective and negotiate better rates.'
limitations: National averages; spot-contract spreads are our arithmetic; no direct broker-margin data.

title: Truckload rates continue surge as CDL regs squeeze driver capacity
claim: TL spot rates ex-fuel +32.4% YoY in Q2 2026, pacing +43% QTD in Q3 (RXO forecast data); RXO economist estimates 20-25% of for-hire TL supply could exit.
excerpt: Paraphrase: spot rates ex-fuel rose 32.4% YoY in Q2 and pacing up 43.0% QTD in Q3.

title: FMCSA's CDL crackdown is fracturing freight networks
claim: Non-domiciled CDL enforcement estimated to remove ~200,000 drivers (~5% of interstate CDL holders); English-proficiency OOS violations ~3% of inspections; non-domiciled carriers exiting or going intrastate.
excerpt: Paraphrase: stricter non-domiciled CDL enforcement estimated to remove nearly 200,000 drivers.
limitations: Via search snippet; estimates contested (JOC reported some analysts attribute spikes partly to seasonality).

title: Cargo theft losses surge to estimated $725 million in 2025
claim: 2025 estimated cargo-theft losses ~$725M (+60%); 3,594 supply-chain crime incidents (flat); confirmed cargo thefts 2,646 (+18%); avg theft $273,990; schemes increasingly use acquired carriers with strong load histories; enforcement may expand distressed carriers available for fraudulent takeovers.
excerpt: Paraphrase: cargo theft becoming 'less opportunistic and more strategic'.
limitations: Fetched page body empty; figures from trade-press summaries (CCJ, Truckinginfo) of the Verisk release. No separate double-brokering loss figure.

title: What Is Freight Broker Factoring? How It Works, Costs, & Types
claim: Shippers typically pay brokers on 30-60+ day terms; broker factoring advances 80-95% within ~24h; fees ~1-5% of invoice per 30 days plus other fees; recourse buyback typically after 60-90 days.
excerpt: Paraphrase: factoring fee roughly 1%-5% of invoice value per 30 days.
limitations: Explainer with vendor-adjacent content; not a market survey.

title: Before You Ask About the Freight Broker Agent - Agency Split
claim: Independent freight agent commission splits commonly 60/40 to 80/20 of gross margin in agent's favor; caps/minimum-margin rules common; agency financial stability matters more than split.
excerpt: Paraphrase: splits range from 60/40 to 80/20.
limitations: Industry blog/marketing; splits corroborated only by other blogs (Trinity Logistics, climbtheladder).

title: Intermodalism: Metropolitan Chicago's built-in economic advantage
claim: Chicago region is the busiest rail-truck intermodal port in the U.S.; ~14.2M TEU through regional intermodal facilities (2012); FHWA citing CMAP: ~25% of U.S. freight railcars and ~50% of intermodal containers/trailers pass through Chicago.
excerpt: Paraphrase: region is the busiest rail-truck intermodal port in the U.S.

claim: N.A. intermodal volume ~+4.6% YTD vs 2025; domestic intermodal +12.6% YoY early Oct; Chicago: limited committed capacity, higher rates, longer transit; railroads expected to take larger rate increases Q1 2027.

title: UIIA Insurance Requirements
claim: Motor carriers must carry trailer-interchange insurance (comprehensive, collision, fire, theft) for non-owned equipment and meet each equipment provider's requirements; UIIA participation needed for rail/port interchange.
excerpt: Trailer Interchange insurance covers physical damage to non-owned equipment while in the Motor Carrier's care, custody and/or control.
limitations: Limits vary by equipment provider; not quantified here.

title: UIIA FAQ

excerpt: Paraphrase: carrier that brokers must register as both a Broker and a Motor Carrier.

claim: Individual license requires U.S. citizenship, age 21+, not a current federal employee, good moral character, passing the Customs Broker License Exam, application with fees, CBP approval.
excerpt: Applicant must 'be a United States citizen at least 21 years old.'
limitations: Page does not state fees, pass mark, CE hours or timelines.

title: Relations with unlicensed persons
claim: Customs broker may not share fees/benefits with unlicensed persons for customs business for others; only exception: broker may compensate a freight forwarder for referrals, with importer notice and direct billing conditions.

title: Supreme Court strikes down IEEPA tariffs: key takeaways for importers

excerpt: Paraphrase: refunds processed through CAPE in the ACE portal, electronic only.
